calls.head: The Bruins hunt better looks than the Red Wings
calls.body: The Bruins wait for good looks, but the Red Wings settle for hopeful ones. Boston is one of the league’s best for shot quality, and Detroit is near the bottom. The more dangerous chances should be the Bruins’.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Pastrňák has a goal and an assist as the Bruins take down the Red Wings
paras: Lucas Raymond opened the scoring for the Red Wings late in the first, and that was all they would get. JJ Peterka tied it 1-1 for Boston early in the second, and Pavel Zacha gave the Bruins the lead on the power play midway through the period. David Pastrňák extended the lead to 3-1 early in the third. Casey Mittelstadt added an empty-net goal with just under a minute left to make it 4-1.

The Bruins outshot the Red Wings 31-21, but the Red Wings’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Jeremy Swayman made 20 saves for the Bruins, and Daniil Tarasov stopped 27 of 30 at the other end.

Only two penalties were called all night, something the league sees about once every 20 games. The Bruins moved to 14-7-1, fourth in the Atlantic, while the Red Wings fell to 8-11-3, seventh in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Bruins won for the first time in four games.
Viktor Arvidsson played his first game against Boston since leaving.
David Pastrňák has a point in all ten of his games against Detroit since 2023-24.
Lucas Raymond has a point in four straight games, with a goal in each of the last three.
